title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Problem Book (问题集). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Problem Book
options.lineage: competition problem sets and solution notebooks, indexed by technique
options.thesis: The blog is a bound problem book: the index and the dated ledger ARE the page. A record is found by technique and by year, and a translation pair is a catalogue cross-reference rather than a language menu.
options.viewport: The book's opening spread, not a hero. A masthead band sets LOTP in condensed caps beside a front-matter line (engineering notes · 2016 → 2026 · written and translated by hand). The left column is the index: techniques with counts, and a year spine 2016 … 2026 that jumps the ledger. The right column is the ledger itself — records grouped under year markers, each row numbered, dated, tagged, and marked 中 only where a twin exists.
options.risk: A ledger of text can read cold. If the masthead is timid and the index sparse this becomes a database instead of a book, and there is no imagery to hide behind.

raised.raise: Every state is named in text and never carried by colour alone: 当前 / current, 已配对 / paired with its Original, 暂无中文 / no Chinese twin.
On narrow screens the plan travels with the section: a slim sticky index bar sits above the ledger instead of the index hiding behind a menu.
Total commitment to a fixed ink set, with one ink reserved for exactly one thing — red only ever marks the record you are on.
State changes land in whole steps: nothing half-faded or half-open, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured as the same states without motion.

options.label: Facing Pages
options.lineage: Loeb-classical facing-page editions and 中英对照 technical translations
options.thesis: The site is a bilingual edition printed in two columns: every record carries its translation beside it, and the language is a column, not a dropdown.
options.viewport: The home page is a table of contents printed in two columns — Original left, 中文 right — entries joined by a rule, with the pair's shared number in the gutter.
options.risk: This is where a bilingual blog most obviously lands, and the honest count works against it: 1 of 15 records has a twin, so a facing-page law exposes 14 empty halves and risks making an Untranslated post look incomplete, which this product forbids.
options.case: My top-ranked grounded candidate. Stronger on the pairing mechanism than the assigned direction; weaker on the answer-first index the primary reader came for.

options.label: Vertical Feed Surface
options.thesis: Each record owns a whole viewport; a right rail of actions; the next record is one snap away and already loaded.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on audience identification — every reader here lives inside a vertical feed all day — and fails on product clarity: a decade of text records needs ten rows in view at once, and this site's GIFs illustrate arguments rather than being the content.
options.kept: The next record is already resolved and waiting: prev/next named by title at the end of every article, never an anonymous arrow back to the list.
options.risk: A media-first shell wearing a text-first record.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.lineage: particle-physics event displays — detector cross-sections, calorimeter wedges
options.thesis: One record as a collision: its tags are tracks radiating outward; pick a track and everything else dims.
options.case: Holds product clarity — isolate-one-tag-and-dim-the-rest is precisely what a tag page should do, and writing confidence as line weight is honest — but loses audience identification (a physicist's instrument, not an engineer's reading material) and would give a long-form text site a dark instrument ground.
options.kept: Isolate-and-dim on tag pages: the current technique solid and labelled in text, the other techniques present but dimmed — never dimmed colour alone.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.case: Fuses poorly: a blog has no atmospheric phases, so light-as-structure would decorate a text record.
options.kept: Named states with text-equivalent labels — colour is never the sole signal.

options.label: Deployable Curved Shell
options.lineage: a single curved crease folding a flat sheet into a rigid shell
options.case: Fuses poorly: one sweeping arc as the compositional law breaks a ledger built for scanning.
options.kept: Plan and section paired on small screens.

options.label: Hatch Show Print
options.lineage: letterpress gig broadsides, wood type in full-width bands
options.case: Fuses poorly: bands forced to fill the measure make a poster, not an index an engineer scans for an answer.
options.kept: A fixed ink set with one ink reserved for one thing.

options.label: Arcade Cabinet
options.lineage: pixel-art arcade screens, scanlines and phosphor bloom
options.case: Fuses poorly: a tile grid and a pixel face tax a reading surface, and the subject's work is not a game screen.
options.kept: Whole-step state changes, no half-finished transitions.

canonCard.label: The Reading Blog, Done Well
canonCard.thesis: The category standard for a personal engineering blog — identity block, clean chronological list, one reading column — executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement every visitor already knows: identity at the top, a chronological list of titles, a calm article column.
canonCard.risk: It is close to what this site is today — safe, familiar, indistinguishable from a good Hugo blog. That is exactly what you asked to leave.
